assumptions: The feature keys and qualifiers GenBank accepts are the current INSDC tables the builder carries.
limits: Builds the files; the submission itself and NCBI's own validation are not run here.
bio.jane/contract.question: What submission set (fasta with source modifiers and a feature table) does NCBI's table2asn take for this record, and what had to be refused or migrated?

description: Turn a record into the SUBMISSION SET NCBI's `table2asn` consumes: a `.fsa` whose defline carries the source modifiers, and a 5-column feature table (`.tbl`) beside it. This is not a GenBank export — GenBank's submission pipeline takes neither a `.gb` nor a plain fasta. Its real work is REFUSING and MIGRATING what GenBank will not accept: twelve feature keys were retired in 2014 in favour of `regulatory` (promoter, terminator and RBS among them, so every plasmid map is affected), a qualifier not on a key's approved list is dropped by name, and an unapproved key is kept as a `misc_feature` carrying its original name. Since December 2024 GenBank has required `collection_date` and `geo_loc_name` on every submission, and both are validated here against the INSDC vocabularies BEFORE a file is written. It WRITES FILES and sends nothing: no account, no key, no upload — `table2asn` stays yours to run, and the submission template it also wants is yours to make.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

collection_date.description: when the sample was collected. MANDATORY on every GenBank submission since December 2024. `DD-Mmm-YYYY`, `Mmm-YYYY`, `YYYY`, an ISO form, or two of them separated by `/` for a range. A construct that was never collected anywhere takes an INSDC missing-value term such as `missing: lab stock`.

genbank.description: the record to submit, as GenBank text. Its features and topology are read from it — wire it from an export, or paste it.

geo_loc_name.description: where the sample came from: a country, ocean or sea from the INSDC vocabulary, optionally `:region` and `, locality`. MANDATORY since December 2024, and it takes the same missing-value terms.

mol_type.description: one of INSDC's two MANDATORY qualifiers on the source key. Omitting it lets table2asn choose, which is a scientific fact picked by a tool.

organism.description: the scientific name of the source organism. `synthetic construct` is a real answer for a built vector, not an absence.

topology.description: circular for a plasmid. With this omitted table2asn writes `linear` into the LOCUS line, so a plasmid is deposited as a linear molecule with no error anywhere. Left empty, the record's own topology is used. Values:  (From the record), circular (Circular), linear (Linear). Advanced.

name: build_genbank_submission

changes.description: every feature the writer migrated, relabelled, refused or stripped a qualifier from, each with the authority's reason. Never empty-because-nothing-was-checked

command.description: the exact table2asn invocation for the set, naming the submission template the user must make first

featureTable.description: the `.tbl` alone, for pasting or diffing

files.description: the submission set: one entry per file, each with its `name` and `text`. The two names share a basename, which is how table2asn pairs them

problems.description: why the set cannot be submitted as it stands — an illegal collection date or a locality outside the vocabulary. Empty means the two mandatory modifiers are good, never that NCBI will be silent

reading.description: what the set is, generated from the record that was written rather than from the request

written.description: features written into the table. Branch on this rather than counting `changes`
